claim: Google v. Oracle (2021) found fair use for copying ~11,500 lines of Java API declaring code (0.4% of the program), assuming copyrightability without deciding it.
evidence: Google copied roughly 11,500 lines of code from the Java SE program. ... To decide no more than is necessary to resolve this case, the Court assumes for argument's sake that the copied lines can be copyrighted, and focuses on whether Google's use of those lines was a 'fair use.'
excerpt:
Argued October 7, 2020—Decided April 5, 2021 Oracle America, Inc., owns a copyright in Java SE, a computer platform that uses the popular Java computer programming language. In 2005, Google acquired Android and sought to build a new software platform for mobile devices.
